q: Fill in the blank: She ____ to school every day.
e: A singular third-person subject in the simple present takes the verb with -s/-es: 'goes'.

q: Fill in the blank: Look! It ____ heavily outside.
e: 'Look!' shows an action happening now, so the present continuous 'is raining' is used.

q: Fill in the blank: By the time we reached the station, the train ____.
e: Of two past actions, the earlier one takes the past perfect: the train had left before we reached.

q: Fill in the blank: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ the match.
e: A real future condition (first conditional) uses the simple present in the if-clause and 'will' + verb in the main clause.

q: Fill in the blank: He ____ in this company since 2015.
e: An action that began in the past and is still continuing, with 'since', takes the present perfect continuous.

q: Choose the correct article: She is ____ honest woman.
e: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (the 'h' is silent), so 'an' is used.

q: Choose the correct article: ____ Ganga is a sacred river of India.
e: The definite article is used before the names of rivers.

q: Choose the correct article: He is ____ university professor.
e: 'University' begins with a consonant 'yu' sound, so 'a' is used.

q: Fill in the blanks: ____ rich should help ____ poor.
e: 'The' + adjective denotes a whole class of people: 'the rich', 'the poor'.

q: Fill in the blank: He has been ill ____ Monday.
e: 'Since' is used with a point of time in the perfect tense; 'for' is used with a period of time.

q: Fill in the blank: The train arrived exactly at its scheduled time; it was ____ time.
e: 'On time' means at the scheduled time; 'in time' means early enough.

q: Fill in the blank: The heavy rain prevented us ____ going out.
e: The verb 'prevent' is followed by 'from' + -ing form.

q: Change into passive voice: Ram writes a letter.
o: A letter was written by Ram.
A letter is written by Ram.
A letter has been written by Ram.
A letter is being written by Ram.
e: Simple present active becomes 'is/are + past participle' in the passive.

q: Change into passive voice: They are building a new bridge.
o: A new bridge is built by them.
A new bridge is being built by them.
A new bridge has been built by them.
A new bridge was being built by them.
e: Present continuous active becomes 'is/are being + past participle' in the passive.

q: Change into passive voice: Who taught you English?
o: By whom you were taught English?
By whom are you taught English?
By whom were you taught English?
e: 'Who' becomes 'By whom', and the simple past takes 'were + past participle' with question order.

q: Change into passive voice: Let him do the work.
o: Let the work is done by him.
The work let be done by him.
Let the work be done by him.
Let the work been done by him.
e: Imperatives with 'let' take the pattern 'Let + object + be + past participle'.

q: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am tired."
o: He said that he is tired.
He said that he was tired.
He said that I was tired.
He said that he had been tired.
e: With a past reporting verb, 'am' changes to 'was' and 'I' changes to 'he'.

q: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, "Please help me."
o: She told me that please help her.
She requested me that help her.
She asked to me to help her.
She requested me to help her.
e: A polite command is reported with 'requested' + object + to-infinitive; 'please' is dropped.

q: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, "The sun rises in the east."
o: The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.
The teacher said that the sun rose in the east.
The teacher said that the sun had risen in the east.
The teacher said that the sun was rising in the east.
e: A universal truth keeps its present tense even when the reporting verb is in the past.

q: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Where do you live?"
o: He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where do I live.
He told me where I lived?
e: In reported questions, the word order becomes that of a statement and the tense moves back: 'where I lived'.

q: Fill in the blank: Each of the boys ____ a prize.
e: 'Each of' takes a singular verb.

q: Fill in the blank: Neither the teacher nor the students ____ present.
e: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here the plural 'students'.

q: Fill in the blank: The quality of the mangoes ____ not good.
e: The real subject is the singular noun 'quality', not 'mangoes'.

q: Spot the error: One of my friend / is a doctor / in Surat. / No error
e: 'One of' is followed by a plural noun: 'One of my friends'.

q: Spot the error: He did not went / to the market / yesterday. / No error
e: After the auxiliary 'did', the base form is used: 'did not go'.

q: Spot the error: Hardly had he reached / the station / than the train left. / No error
e: 'Hardly' is followed by 'when', not 'than': 'when the train left'.

q: Spot the error: The furniture in this room / are very expensive / and old-fashioned. / No error
e: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb: 'is very expensive'.

q: Fill in the blank: Ravi is taller ____ his brother.
e: Comparative adjectives such as 'taller' are followed by 'than'.

q: Fill in the blank: She is one of those women who ____ always ready to help.
e: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural 'women', so the verb is plural.

q: Choose the correct question tag: He is a doctor, ____?
e: A positive statement with 'is' takes the negative tag 'isn't he?'.
